task_name: The real terminal, opened at start-up

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each has production lines behind it. (1) '`make run-backend` opens a real PTY': the Makefile's run-backend runs `node backend/src/infrastructure/ct-api.ts`, and ct-api.ts now imports `spawn` from `node-pty`, builds `PtyLiveSessions` with it and calls `liveSessions.open()` before the ApiServer is constructed; `backend/package.json` carries the dependency so the import resolves. (2) 'the cabin can list': `listLiveSessions: new ListLiveSessions({ liveSessions })` is handed to ApiServer, which mounts `SessionsRoute.handledBy(this.listLiveSessions!)` on `SessionsRoute.PATH` (api-server.ts:231-236), so the opened session appears in GET /sessions. (3) 'it outlives every watcher': measured by the second new test, which stops the only watcher, then writes into the session and sees it answer, and finds it still listed. Nothing the objective names is missing from the diff.

The TDD line asks for `it('a real terminal prints into the scrollback and answers what is written to it')` — 'the real node-pty is injected as the spawn, echo is written into it and the scrollback ends up carrying what it echoed'. The test in the diff is that test: `RealCabin.opening` constructs PtyLiveSessions with `spawn` taken from the real `node-pty` module (no double anywhere in the file), the input is `sessions.write({ session, text: `echo ${token}\n` })`, and the assertion is `expect(watch.printed).toContain(token)` — `printed` being the scrollback PtyLiveSessions keeps. Same assertion, same input, same expected value as the written phrase. The token is minted per test as `ct-real-pty-<uuid>`, so the substring it matches on is distinctive rather than loose.

Task 3 declares no `Contract (path):` block; it declares a `Call site (backend/src/infrastructure/ct-api.ts):` block and a Configuration paragraph, and both are literal. The call site is reproduced symbol for symbol: `new PtyLiveSessions({ spawn, shell: environment.SHELL, cwd: process.cwd(), env: environment, newId: randomUUID, stderr: (line) => process.stderr.write(line) })` followed by `liveSessions.open()` — same parameter names, same order, same expressions (`randomUUID` was already imported at ct-api.ts:3). The Configuration paragraph asks for four things and the diff does all four: `"node-pty": "1.0.0"` in `dependencies` with no caret (package.json and the lockfile's root both read exactly `1.0.0`, and the lock entry carries `hasInstallScript: true` with `nan`, which is the build-from-source path P-4 wants); the lockfile regenerated; `import { spawn } from 'node-pty'` in ct-api.ts; and `listLiveSessions: new ListLiveSessions({ liveSessions })` passed to ApiServer, whose declared key is `listLiveSessions?: ListLiveSessions | null` (api-server.ts:85). The construction sits before the `new ApiServer({...})` call, as the paragraph requires.

Rows the diff bears on, each implemented with the stated value. P-4 (node-pty pinned to 1.0.0, no caret, so the build is from source and spawn-helper stays executable): package.json reads `"node-pty": "1.0.0"` and the control `test -x backend/node_modules/node-pty/build/Release/spawn-helper` is in the task's verification. P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session; ct-api.ts opens the one terminal at start-up and owns it): the diff adds `liveSessions.open()` in the entrypoint and adds no POST/DELETE route for sessions. P-1 (LiveSessions is synchronous): `open()` is called without await and `ListLiveSessions.execute()` returns without a promise. P-6 ($SHELL -il in the backend's own working directory, fallback /bin/sh): the entrypoint passes `shell: environment.SHELL, cwd: process.cwd(), env: environment` and the constants live in the adapter. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript): the new test file is `.ts`. P-8 (English everywhere but product copy): every new identifier, test name and stderr line is English. P-2, P-5, P-7, P-9 and the D-rows about gates, cmux and the conductor are untouched by this diff, which is compliance. No row is reopened.

EXEMPLARS. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/tool-runner-real-process.test.ts` is the named exemplar for 'a test that spawns for real, with the suffix that says so', and the new file matches its idiom: the `-real-process.test.ts` suffix, helper types instead of loose functions (`Node` there; `RealTerminals`, `RealCabin`, `Echoed` here), cleanup in `afterEach`, and real processes rather than doubles. One divergence, declared rather than reported: the exemplar names its tests in snake_case (`what_the_tool_prints_comes_back_with_the_code_that_says_it_went_well`) and the diff names them as spaced sentences. The task's `**TDD:**` and `**Tests:**` lines prescribe the spaced names verbatim and `ct-step controls` greps the staged files for those exact strings, so a snake_case name would have failed a control of the plan — the clash is between the plan's control and the exemplar, and the implementer answers for neither; task 2's already-committed `pty-live-sessions.test.ts` uses the same spaced style, so the slice is at least coherent with itself. `probed-tool-sessions.ts`/`tool-runner.ts` idiom — collaborators by name through the constructor — is what the new ct-api.ts lines do.

REPO RULES. `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`: 'This suite launches real processes by design. Every spawned child is killed in afterEach, not after the assertion' — honoured, `RealTerminals` keeps every pty it handed out in `#opened` and `afterEach(() => realTerminals.killAll())` kills them whether or not the assertion passed; 'The fast subset is npx vitest run --exclude "**/*-real-process.test.ts"' — honoured by the filename; 'A relative import names the extension the file really has' — `'../../src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts'`, `'./pty-live-sessions.ts'`, `'../application/queries/list-live-sessions.ts'`; erasable syntax only — nothing in the diff is an enum, namespace, decorator or parameter property, and typecheck is green. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: everything the diff writes is English and no control is routed around.

CT YARDSTICK. `style.md`: no comment or docstring in the new file, and no free function at module level — every function hangs off `RealTerminals`, `RealCabin` or `Echoed`, the inline arrows being call arguments. `architecture.md`: the entrypoint is 'the only place that assembles the dependency graph: it picks the concrete adapters and injects them' — ct-api.ts picks the `PtyLiveSessions` adapter and injects it into the `ListLiveSessions` use case, which declares its dependency as the port type; no new concept is smuggled into an old file, the three lines are wiring, which is what an entrypoint is for. `boundaries.md`'s cap rule has no subject: a long-lived interactive terminal is not a call waiting for an answer, and the adapter itself was task 2's diff. `simplicity.md`: 'Observability answers to a reader who exists' — the `stderr` sink passed in has the reader the plan names, whoever runs `make run-backend` and wants to tell a live cabin terminal from a dead one. `decisions.md`: the literal `'plans in flight:'` now appears twice in ct-api-real-process.test.ts (the wait predicate and the assertion's expected text), but that is a test's own wait condition beside its own assertion, not a business rule decided in two places; no business change forces touching both. `domain.md` has no subject — the diff adds no port, value object or exception. Delivery shape: no document of either yardstick prescribes a delivery pattern for this change; it is purely additive (a new dependency, wiring lines, a constructor key task 1 already declared as optional) and leaves no call site on an old path.

DEFECTS.MD, RULE BY RULE. (1) Closed vocabulary instead of loose strings and booleans — no subject: the diff adds no value that classifies anything and no dispatch; `environment.SHELL` is a program path, not a classifier. (2) No raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: nothing the diff adds returns a map; `ListLiveSessions` returns the `ListLiveSessionsResult` object it already declared, and the options object handed to node-pty's `spawn` is an argument at the outer edge, not the return value of logic. (3) Two fields that have to agree, sentinel included — no subject: `shell` is typed `string | undefined` and the absence is carried in the type with `?? FALLBACK_SHELL`, not as an empty-string sentinel, and the diff adds no flag repeating another field. (4) Errors named for what happens, not for where — no subject: the diff raises and declares no error.

The diff has exactly one `-` line in a test file: `-      if (started.saidLater().length > 0) break` in `ct-api-real-process.test.ts`, replaced by `if (started.saidLater().includes('plans in flight:')) break`. That line is the polling condition of the `Entrypoint.recovering` helper, not an assertion, a case or a test, and the rewrite makes it strictly stricter: it used to break out of the wait on the first byte of stderr, and now it waits for the recovery diagnostic itself. The assertion it serves is untouched — `expect(started.saidLater()).toContain(`plans in flight: ${orphan}`)` at ct-api-real-process.test.ts:267 — and it can still fail for the reason its name gives: if recovery never prints, the loop exhausts its sixty 100ms rounds and the assertion fails on the stderr it actually got. This is a repair, not a weakening: opening the pty at start-up now writes `live session … opened` to stderr before `recovery.recover()` runs, which is exactly the first-byte the old heuristic mistook for the recovery line. No other assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten anywhere in the diff, and the brief's amended `**Files:**` accounts for the file.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. The pty is opened by `liveSessions.open()` in `ct-api.ts`, it is listed because `ListLiveSessions` is wired into ApiServer, and it survives a watcher because `PtyLiveSessions.watch` returns a `stop` that deletes only that watcher. The new test file contains no mock, no stub and no hard-coded expected value standing in for production: its expected value is a UUID token minted at run time and asserted to have travelled out through the real `node-pty` master, back through `onData` and into the scrollback the adapter keeps. Noted and not a finding: the three entrypoint wiring lines have no test of their own in this diff — the task's `**Tests:**` names only the two adapter-level real-process tests, so a GET /sessions assertion in the entrypoint suite would have been code no sentence of the task asked for.

Inside the declared files the diff writes only what the task asks. ct-api.ts gains two imports and six lines, every one of them dictated by the Call site block and the Configuration paragraph; package.json gains one dependency at the pinned value; the lockfile gains only the `node-pty` and `nan` entries that pin implies. Nothing in `### Out of scope` is touched: the eight existing endpoints keep their paths and answers, no endpoint opens or kills a session, nothing resizes a terminal, no second frame kind appears, and no command beyond the login shell is chosen. THE AMENDMENT: the plan hunk is one line, adding `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/ct-api-real-process.test.ts` (modify) to this task's `**Files:**`. It adds a route rather than removing one; it leaves `**Objective:**`, `**TDD:**`, `**Tests:**` and all four `**Verification:**` commands exactly as committed, so it disarms no control. It is justified by a sentence of this task: `npm --prefix backend test   # expected: exit 0`. Opening the pty at start-up puts a stderr line ahead of the recovery diagnostic, which breaks the pre-existing entrypoint test's wait heuristic, so that command cannot be green without touching that file — and the alternative was touching a file the plan did not declare. Declaring it and repairing one polling predicate is the narrower move.

Two new tests, both with the three properties. DETERMINISTIC: no clock or date in any assertion, no network, no path outside what the pty needs, no sleep standing in for synchronisation — the wait is on the pty's own `onData`, and the randomness is a per-test `ct-real-pty-<uuid>` token whose only job is to be unique, never to decide the verdict. The host's `$SHELL` is a real dependency, but it is the one P-6 prescribes and the assertion rides on the pty's round trip rather than on any particular shell's output. ISOLATED: `beforeEach` mints a fresh `RealTerminals`, each test opens its own session with its own token, nothing is written to disk, no port or fixed directory is taken for granted, no order is needed, and `afterEach(() => realTerminals.killAll())` kills every pty the test spawned even when the assertion has already failed — which is `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`'s own rule, 'Every spawned child is killed in afterEach, not after the assertion'. VERIFIES REAL BEHAVIOUR: there is no double in the file at all; `expect(watch.printed).toContain(token)` is on the scrollback the production adapter maintains after bytes crossed a real pty, and `expect(sessions.find(session.id)).not.toBeNull()` is on the map the adapter empties in `onExit`; neither would pass with the diff's `package.json` dependency reverted, because the module would not import. FINER HALF: I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md`. None of the five anti-patterns bites — nothing is mocked, no test-only method was added to a production class. The one thing I can pin is the skill's 'Minimal | One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' against `'a real terminal prints into the scrollback and answers what is written to it'`; I am leaving it out of the findings because the task's `**TDD:**` line prescribes that name verbatim and `ct-step controls` greps the staged file for that exact string, so splitting it would have failed a control of the plan. The implementer also declares that both assertions were broken by hand, seen to fail for their own stated reason and the file restored byte-identical, which is the declaration `conventions/testing.md` asks a judge to read.
